## Outcome
Reproduce one bounded GitHub issue/PR conversation → attributed agent result through the existing Reach preparation boundary. Use this concrete example to define the small provider seam before expanding integrations.

**Primary:** Kiran (@Kiranchaudhary537). **Partners:** Nav for Reach/workflow and Anshuk for backend/privacy boundaries; Chirayu for the visible result and acceptance.  
**Selection:** side quest after the web/phone main work #154/#159 and first Scout study #155. Campaign priority is **GitHub → Gmail → YouTube**. This changes the candidate plan's Gmail-first qualification sequence, not its delivery/custody/recovery requirements. Broader outcomes remain in #62.

## First result
- [ ] Pin the current source revision and reproduce the GitHub request-preparation path. Reuse the current provider builder and exact connection/partition/target policy; identify which parts currently do no network, authentication or delivery.
- [ ] Choose one public repository and one issue/PR conversation. Bound reads, pagination and budgets; preserve provider/instance/object identity, observation/version information and attribution in the common Graph/UI result envelope. Start with fixtures and distinguish any separately selected live public read.
- [ ] Demonstrate a useful attributed answer or local proposed timeline comment. Include wrong-target refusal, hostile/untrusted comment text, pagination/budget exhaustion and unavailable/interrupted reads. Source text supplies data, not authority to execute code or write elsewhere.
- [ ] Map the missing authenticated-read seam: selected repository/operation access, GitHub App installation and token custody, revocation/removal, rate limits and secret-free observations. Request construction does not prove a live authorized connector.
- [ ] Record one narrow next implementation and give another participant reproducible steps. Actual comment delivery remains separate until durable intent, review/current authority, attempt fencing and unknown-outcome reconciliation are implemented.
- [ ] Produce a short Google follow-on note: shared account/OAuth registration, callback validation, token custody/refresh and reconnect machinery; distinct Gmail mailbox and YouTube channel identities, operations, scopes, quotas and local policy. Define how one service disconnects without unexpectedly revoking another combined grant.

## Small reusable seam
Keep the concrete GitHub implementation behind a narrow typed operation boundary with provider-qualified identity and explicit supported capabilities. The current GitHub-specific target/builder must not be represented as an already portable adapter. Do not implement a universal forge framework before another real operation justifies it.

**Git source is different from forge correspondence.** Git objects/remotes may be the right initial mechanism for source acquisition, but they do not provide issue/PR comments, reviews or collaboration state. Source canon and release trust follow [ADR 17](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/adr/17-packaging.md#forge-neutral-source-trust). Forgejo/Gitea are later adapter candidates; Radicle may also require a separate source/collaboration decision. Do not assume API, identifier or review-model compatibility. Record unsupported capabilities instead of hiding them behind a GitHub-shaped universal interface.

Gmail and YouTube may share Google account/auth machinery without sharing an unrestricted permission set. A Gmail compose grant can permit sending; a local draft-only policy still needs enforcement. YouTube correspondence may fit Reach, while publishing a finished video belongs to Broadcast's release contract. Choose a concrete YouTube operation before selecting its owner or API scopes; it is the lowest-priority provider follow-on here.

## Boundaries and owners
No code execution, Git push, merge/release, formal review, Actions/status mutation or background monitoring is required. Privacy/anonymization and egress follow #25/#28/#62; use public/synthetic material for the initial proof. Review the shared seam early, then use agents for the bounded candidate; one review-ready implementation per pair remains the limit.

Start from the [connected-work candidate](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/compositions/reach/connected-work/index.md), [forge boundary](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/compositions/reach/forge.md), [GitHub profile](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/compositions/reach/connected-work/github.md), [account lifecycle](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/docs/compositions/reach/connected-work/accounts.md) and [request builders](https://github.com/hexanomicon/lychd/blob/main/src/lychd/compositions/reach/connected/providers.py). Candidate contracts are not delivery evidence.

Provider references: [GitHub timeline comments](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/issues/comments), [Google OAuth and combined grants](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/web-server), [Gmail scopes](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes), [YouTube authorization](https://developers.google.com/youtube/data/guides/authentication).
